newsitem.title: FRANCE: French truckers protest for better work conditions.
newsitem.headline: French truckers protest for better work conditions.

text.p: Truckers caused traffic chaos across France on Monday by blocking roads in protests demanding more money and shorter working hours.
Union leaders urged members to continue their protests on Tuesday, accusing Transport Minister Bernard Pons of failing to meet their demands at a meeting in Paris on Monday afternoon.
"I appeal to people to keep up what we've done today, that is blockades and maybe strikes," said Roger Poletti, a leader of the Force Ouvriere union.
He said Pons had made some interesting points on secondary issues but offered little more.
The truckers, heading the latest in a spate of labour disruptions in France in recent months, are also demanding the right to retire at 55 rather than 60.
Police reported heavy traffic jams around the southwestern city of Bordeaux, where Prime Minister Alain Juppe is mayor, after truck drivers blocked the three main access roads.

In eastern France, protesters cut off a bridge connecting France and Germany over the river Rhine at Strasbourg by parking between 150 and 200 trucks on either side of the border. They allowed only private cars through.

In Toulouse, motorists had a free motorway ride as protesters lifted toll gates. The winter's first snowfall worsened disruption in the Lyon and Valence areas. Other drivers stopped work, leaving their trucks outside haulage companies.
There were also roadblocks near several other major cities including Marseille in the south, Caen, Le Mans and Rennes in the west, and Troyes in the east.
Traffic was disrupted earlier in several cities by demonstrators demanding cuts in taxes on diesel fuel.
Ten days ago haulage company bosses snarled traffic in several cities, winning a government pledge to keep down increases in taxes on diesel fuel.
